core.title: Render a responsive e2e test at every declared viewport width
core.given: An e2e test identified as responsive: its test URN carries the stack's responsive code (profile: urn.test), or its file base name has a `responsive`/`resp` token (tokens split only on the stack's name-separator characters, profile: idiom.name_token_separators; never directory names or arbitrary substrings).
core.when: You write or change that spec.
core.then: Render the page at every viewport width the stack declares for responsive rendering (profile: idiom.viewports), not at a single width.
prefer: Iterate the declared widths and render at each one, asserting at every width that the page does not overflow horizontally.

Set the viewport width for each declared width through one of the stack's recognized width-setting forms (profile: idiom.viewport_setting_forms) — a per-spec viewport option, an in-test viewport switch, or by iterating the declared list of widths.
avoid: Rendering at only one of the declared widths, e.g. by picking a single element of the widths list.

Measuring the stack's horizontal-overflow measure (profile: idiom.overflow_measure) without passing it — directly or through a value measured from it — to the stack's test assertion (profile: idiom.test_assertion); the spec MUST do so, so the test fails when the page overflows horizontally (a separate obligation; the realization records the split).
core.why: A screen that works on a desktop can be unusable on a phone; rendering at each declared width and asserting the document never scrolls sideways is the least that proves it fits.
evidence: The stack's responsive-harness check reports no finding for the spec.
A reviewer sees every declared width (profile: idiom.viewports, including the stack's defaults) rendered via the stack's recognized width-setting forms (profile: idiom.viewport_setting_forms).
A reviewer sees the stack's overflow measure (profile: idiom.overflow_measure), directly or through a value measured from it, inside the stack's test assertion (profile: idiom.test_assertion).
verification: A spec is in scope only if BOTH hold: the file is a browser-driven e2e test per the profile's e2e-test kinds, AND it carries a responsive identifier — the responsive code in its test URN (profile: urn.test), or a `responsive`/`resp` token in its base name. Base-name tokens are exactly the segments split on the stack's name-separator characters (profile: idiom.name_token_separators); directory names and arbitrary substrings never count, and the token identifier only counts together with the browser-spec fact.

What counts as a browser spec comes from the profile (e2e-test name pattern run by the stack's browser driver, or a journey binding in the file header), so a misnamed spec is still judged; a unit test that merely mentions a journey URN inside a string is not one.

Declared widths come from the stack's viewport declaration (profile: idiom.viewports), including the stack's defaults when none are declared; the check accepts the stack's recognized width-setting forms (profile: idiom.viewport_setting_forms) for rendering at a given width, and picking one element of a widths list counts as rendering one width only.

The horizontal-overflow assertion is a second, independent obligation preserved by this realization (see its split suggestion): the spec must pass the stack's overflow measure (profile: idiom.overflow_measure) — directly or through a value measured from it — to the stack's test assertion (profile: idiom.test_assertion), so the test fails when the page overflows horizontally.

Scan scope: the check never scans vendored or generated trees. This rule's checker owns the exact classification of which trees are excluded (the realization states its exact list); this is a scan-scope exclusion, not an agent waiver.
The detector, validator and finding ids of this rule are realization details; the core names the check generically.

profileRequirements.meaning: What counts as a browser-driven e2e test (a browser spec) in this stack, including misnamed files that still count via a journey binding.
profileRequirements.bunValue: browser_spec: a `*.e2e.ts` file run by Playwright, or any test file whose header comments carry a journey marker (`// Train:`, `// Journey:`, `// URN: test:train:…`, `// URN: test:journey:…`); a unit test that merely mentions a journey URN in a string is not one

profileRequirements.meaning: The e2e-test file name pattern whose absence makes a file 'misnamed'.
The header-marker syntax by which a test file binds itself to a journey, which keeps a misnamed file in scope.
profileRequirements.bunValue: `// Train:`, `// Journey:`, `// URN: test:train:…`, `// URN: test:journey:…`

profileRequirements.meaning: The URN a test carries and the classification codes it may carry, in particular the code that marks a test as responsive.
profileRequirements.bunValue: a test URN (e.g. `test:train:…`, `test:journey:…`) may carry harness codes; the responsive code is `RESP`

profileRequirements.meaning: The viewport widths a responsive e2e test must render, where the stack declares them, and the default when undeclared.
The stack's recognized constructs for rendering a browser spec at a given viewport width: the per-spec viewport option, the in-test viewport switch, and iteration over a list of widths.
profileRequirements.bunValue: `page.setViewportSize({ width })`, a `viewport: { width }` option, or iterating a list of widths (`for (const w of [...])`, `LIST.forEach`, `LIST.map`)

profileRequirements.meaning: The measurement construct a responsive browser test must use to detect horizontal overflow of the rendered page, and the derived forms that count as the same measurement.
profileRequirements.bunValue: `scrollWidth`, used directly or through a variable measured from it

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack's assertion construct inside a test, which the measured overflow value must reach for it to be checked.

The exact characters on which a file's base name is split into tokens for name-token identification, and the fact that only base-name tokens (never directory names or arbitrary substrings) are matched.
profileRequirements.bunValue: split on `.`, `-`, `_` only; matched against tokens of the file's basename, never against directory names or arbitrary substrings

proposedKeys.meaning: URN shape of a test file and the classification codes it may carry (here: the code that marks a test as responsive).
proposedKeys.bunValue: a test URN (e.g. `test:train:…`, `test:journey:…`) may carry harness codes; the responsive code is `RESP`
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: urn.<artifact> params cover component, acceptance, smoke_acceptance, train, wmbt, wagon, feature and journey, but no key describes the URN carried by a test file or its harness codes.

proposedKeys.meaning: The viewport widths a responsive e2e test must render, where the stack declares them, and the default when undeclared.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: No vocabulary key carries browser-harness configuration values; roots.config only locates the roots/profile file and says nothing about nested harness settings such as viewport widths.

proposedKeys.meaning: The stack's recognized constructs for rendering a browser spec at a given viewport width: the per-spec viewport option, the in-test viewport switch, and iteration over a list of widths.
proposedKeys.bunValue: `page.setViewportSize({ width })`, a `viewport: { width }` option, or iterating a list of widths (`for (const w of [...])`, `LIST.forEach`, `LIST.map`)
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: No vocabulary key describes how a stack's browser test sets the viewport width; idiom.viewports carries the widths themselves, not the rendering constructs.

proposedKeys.meaning: The measurement construct a responsive browser test must use to detect horizontal overflow of the rendered page, including the derived values that count as the same measurement.
proposedKeys.bunValue: `scrollWidth`, used directly or through a variable measured from it
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: idiom.nesting_measure measures source-code nesting depth; no idiom or tooling key names the document-overflow measurement of a rendered page.

proposedKeys.meaning: The stack's assertion construct inside a test, which a measured value must be passed to for it to be checked.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: tooling.test_runner names the runner, not the assertion construct; no idiom key describes how a test asserts a value.

proposedKeys.meaning: The exact characters on which a file's base name is split into tokens for name-token identification (base-name tokens only, never directory names or arbitrary substrings).
proposedKeys.bunValue: split on `.`, `-`, `_` only; matched against tokens of the file's basename, never against directory names or arbitrary substrings
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: suffix.<file_kind> lists suffixes and name patterns but does not define token boundaries; no other key describes how a file name is tokenized.
